title: Uniform proper heart bound on the constructible weak Serre coproduct closure over a qcqs base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, and a finite commutative ring $A$ annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda$ be one of $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$: $A$ is discrete and the other rings have their induced $\ell$-adic topologies, as in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, and let $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ be proper morphisms. For $T=X,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$, with ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A_T)$ and total right derived module-object pushforward $Rf_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Use the small-site and indexing universe of [def-weil-size-convention].
Let $\mathcal P_X$ be the intersection of all classes of objects of $\mathcal A_X$ which contain zero and every constructible module in the finite constant scalar-model sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and are closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between members, extensions, and all small coproducts computed in $\mathcal A_X$. Here extension closure means that the middle object of a short exact sequence belongs to the class whenever both end objects do. There is an integer $d\geq0$, independent of $M$, such that
$$H^r(Rf_*(M[0]))=0\qquad(M\in\mathcal P_X,\ r>d).$$
The symbol $M[0]$ denotes the complex concentrated in degree zero. The statement concerns only such heart objects. No assumption of derived completeness, invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes, existence of a field of definition, Noetherianity, or finite dimension of $S$ is made.

proof.text: Since $q$ is proper it is quasi-compact. Take a finite affine open cover of the quasi-compact $S$; each inverse image is quasi-compact by the finite-type definition, so their finite union $Y$ is quasi-compact. Properness of $f$ makes it finite type. The finite-type fibre-dimension theorem supplies $e\in\mathbf N$ such that $\dim X_y\leq e$ for every $y\in Y$. Every fibre is finite type over $\kappa(y)$, and dimension is unchanged under a field extension. Thus the same $e$ bounds every geometric fibre of $f$ and of every base change of $f$. Fix $d=2e+2\geq0$ once and for all.

source.place: Refinement proof (2), first paragraph: direct-sum preservation on the ordinary ambient localizing hull; local geometric inputs for the uniform heart estimate before the lower-tail passage.

proof.text: For any scheme map $a:T\to X$, $a^*$ sends $\mathcal P_X$ into $\mathcal P_T$. Indeed it is additive exact, so preserves zero, kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences. Its adjunction to $a_*$ makes it preserve the small coproducts. The constructible-preimage lemma applies: to check retrocompactness of the inverse image of a retrocompact open, cover any affine source open by finitely many affine opens mapping into affine target opens; the target open in each of those is a finite union of principal opens, whose inverse images are principal. Thus inverse images preserve the required constructible subsets. Pulling back the finite locally closed strata consequently gives a finite constructible stratification; on the pullback of a scalar-model trivializing cover the model is still $\Lambda\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$ for the very same finitely presented scalar module $P$, since the pulled-back coefficient map is an isomorphism. Thus it preserves the specified constructible generators, not merely arbitrary finite presentations. The class of $M$ such that $a^*M\in\mathcal P_T$ therefore has every closure property in the intersection defining $\mathcal P_X$. Minimality gives the assertion.

proof.text:
Fix $M\in\mathcal P_X$ and an affine w-contractible object $W\to Y$ of the small pro-étale site. Apply the proper closed-fibre rigidity theorem to $f,M,W$. It supplies the reduced closed-point scheme $C\hookrightarrow W$: $C$ is affine, zero-dimensional and w-contractible with separably closed residue fields. With $X_C=X\times_YC$ and $a:X_C\to X$ it supplies the actual isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$
$$R\Gamma(X\times_YW,M)\simeq R\Gamma((X_C)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},a^*M).$$
The left side is derived evaluation on the object $X\times_YW$ of the original $X$-site. Thus no substitution of ordinary geometric stalks for arbitrary pro-étale module objects is involved.

proof.text:
The morphism $h:X_C\to C$ is proper by base-change stability. A geometric fibre of $h$ is the base extension of the corresponding fibre of $f$, so Step 1 bounds its dimension by $e$. Step 2 gives $a^*M\in\mathcal P_{X_C}$. Apply the absolute profinite-family cohomological-dimension estimate with this $C,h,e,a^*M$. It gives $H^rR\Gamma((X_C)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},a^*M)=0$ for $r>2e+2=d$. Taking cohomology of the isomorphism of Step 3 gives
$$H^r(X\times_YW,M)=0\qquad(r>d).$$

proof.text: For each $r>d$ consider the abelian presheaf $V\mapsto H^r(X\times_YV,M)$ on $Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$. The bounded-below higher-direct-image presheaf theorem identifies its sheafification with the underlying abelian sheaf of $H^r(Rf_*(M[0]))$. To apply it to the actual module-object composite, use the exact internal-to-section-module equivalences. An injective resolution of $M$ in the source module category computes the actual direct image; before and after scalar restriction its underlying section complex at $V$ is exactly $I^\bullet(X\times_YV)$. Scalar restriction changes only the action and is exact, so these give the same underlying cohomology sheaf as the theorem with target coefficient ring $f_*\Lambda_X$. Every $V$ has a covering by affine w-contractible $W$; on each such $W$ the presheaf is zero by Step 4. Its sheafification is therefore zero. A module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf is zero. This proves the required vanishing for every $M\in\mathcal P_X$ with the fixed $d$ of Step 1.
